headline: Seasons exist because Earth tilts—a 23.5-degree angle changes everything
universal_truth: Small tilts can have enormous consequences over time
fun_facts: Earth's 23.5-degree tilt causes seasons—if we were straight up and down, weather would be constant
When it's summer in the Northern Hemisphere, it's winter in the Southern—and vice versa
The seasons aren't caused by Earth being closer to the Sun—we're actually closest in January
discussion_questions: What small 'tilts' in your life have had big consequences?
How do you adapt to the changing seasons of life—not just weather?
What would be lost if seasons didn't exist?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Summer and winter, spring and fall—we take seasons for granted. But they exist only because Earth is tilted. Just 23.5 degrees, and we get snow in January, beaches in July. That tiny tilt changes everything about life on this planet.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Many people think summer happens when Earth is closer to the Sun. But that's wrong—we're actually closest in January! So what really causes the temperature difference between summer and winter?
cliff.prompt: What causes summer to be warmer than winter?

options.text: Earth's tilt means summer sunlight hits more directly and for longer each day
options.response: Exactly. Tilt determines the angle and duration of sunlight—that's what creates warmth.

options.text: The Sun produces more energy during summer months
options.response: The Sun stays constant—what changes is our angle to it...

q1.title: The 23.5-Degree Secret
q1.script: Earth's axis is tilted 23.5 degrees relative to its orbit. During summer, your hemisphere tilts toward the Sun—sunlight hits more directly and the days are longer. During winter, you tilt away—sunlight comes at an angle and days are shorter.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "The 23.5-Degree Secret"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Opposite Hemispheres
q2.script: When the Northern Hemisphere tilts toward the Sun, the Southern tilts away. That's why Australia has Christmas in summer while Canada has it in winter. The two halves of Earth are always in opposite seasons.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Not About Distance
q3.script: Earth is 3 million miles closer to the Sun in January than July. If distance caused seasons, January would be warmest—but it's winter in the north. The angle of sunlight matters far more than distance.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: A small tilt—just 23.5 degrees—creates the difference between life and death, harvest and famine, growth and dormancy. Small changes in orientation can have enormous effects over time.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 42. Tomorrow, we'll explore why we have day and night. Until then, consider: what small tilts in your perspective might change everything?
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Life Seasons - Recognize Your Cycle
growTrack.learning_objective: Identify what 'season' you're in personally and professionally
growTrack.activity: Consider: are you in a spring (new growth), summer (abundance), fall (harvesting), or winter (rest/dormancy) in different areas of your life? Name them. Each season has its purpose—honor where you are.
